cards.text: Josiah, king of Judah, keeps the Passover to the LORD in Jerusalem, and the Passover lamb is slaughtered on the fourteenth day of the first month. Friend, I once tried to organize six cookie cutters on one counter and it nearly took me OUT. This man is organizing a whole nation.

cards.question: Josiah gets the priests ready for the service of the house of the LORD. Besides appointing them to their duties, what does he do for them?

cards.text: Then Josiah turns to the Levites, the ones who taught all Israel. He tells them to put the holy ark in the temple built by Solomon, and then serve the LORD their God and His people Israel.

cards.question: Josiah tells the Levites the ark is still to be carried around on their shoulders.
Josiah tells the Levites to prepare by families in their divisions, following the instructions written by David king of Israel and ___ his son.

cards.text: Josiah's plan is tighter than my oven timer. The Levites are to stand in the Holy Place by family divisions, slaughter the Passover lambs and consecrate themselves.

cards.question: Josiah tells the Levites to make preparations for somebody besides themselves. Who?
Josiah says the Levites make all these preparations so the people can carry out the word of the LORD given by Moses.

cards.text: Now, a Passover for everybody who shows up takes animals. A LOT of animals, friend, more than all the chocolate chips I've ever owned, and I have owned a SHAMEFUL amount of chocolate chips.

cards.question: Josiah gives 30,000 lambs and goats plus 3,000 bulls for the Passover offerings. Where do they come from?

answers.text: A new tax on the people

cards.text: And the king's not the only one giving, because his officials chip in willingly too. Hilkiah, Zechariah and Jehiel, chief officials of the house of God, give the priests 2,600 Passover offerings and 300 bulls, and the officers of the Levites give the Levites 5,000 Passover offerings and 500 bulls.
So the service is ready: priests in their places, Levites in their divisions, all by the king's command. Then the Passover lambs are slaughtered, and everybody's got a job.

cards.question: As the Passover lambs are slaughtered, the priests skin the animals while the Levites splatter the blood.

cards.text: They set aside the burnt offerings for the families to offer to the LORD, as it is written in the Book of Moses, and they do the same with the bulls. Then it's time to cook, which, I'm not gonna lie to you, is my FAVORITE part of anything.

cards.question: How are the Passover animals cooked, according to the regulation?
The other holy offerings are boiled in pots, kettles and bowls, then left there until the next morning before the people get any.

cards.text: Everybody's been served, but the priests, the descendants of Aaron, are still offering burnt offerings and fat until nightfall. That's me on a big order day: every cookie box in the bakery packed except mine.

cards.question: The priests are busy at the altar until nightfall. Who makes preparations for them?

cards.text: Meanwhile, the singers, the descendants of Asaph, are at their stations, just as David, Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun the king's seer commanded. And the gatekeepers stay right at their gates.

cards.question: The gatekeepers don't need to leave their posts at the gates. Why not?

answers.text: Their fellow Levites prepare for them
They fast through the whole Passover
The king sends their share to the gates

cards.text: So on that day the entire service of the LORD is carried out, the Passover and the burnt offerings on the altar, just as King Josiah commanded. I can't get through ONE Saturday without forgetting the sprinkles, and this man pulled off a whole nation's Passover.

cards.question: The Israelites who are there also observe the Passover, and then the Feast of Unleavened Bread for ___ days.
Israel hasn't seen a Passover like this one since the days of which prophet?
One of the earlier kings of Israel observed a Passover just like Josiah's.

cards.text: All of this happens in the eighteenth year of Josiah's reign. Hold that thought, friend, because Josiah's story isn't finished yet.

findings.problem: Card 3 already tells the baker the temple was 'built by Solomon,' and this blank asks for David's son. That hands over the answer Solomon before the question is asked.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'Josiah's plan is tighter than my oven timer' has no clear shared action between a well-ordered plan and an oven timer. An adult would likely say 'huh?'

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: In 35:6, the BSB leaves open who carries out the word of the LORD: the Levites or the countrymen. The statement settles it as 'so the people can carry out,' and makes it Josiah's stated reason for 'all these preparations.'

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Asaph and Heman appear here for the first time and are only named. The card never says simply who they are. Jeduthun is identified as the king's seer, but they are not.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says the Israelites observe the Passover 'and then' the Feast of Unleavened Bread. The BSB says 'as well as' and gives no order between the two.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
